Briefing (2026-11-20, main c633fbc6) for cutting cold-start cost of a default run (checker on, `--load-dependencies`) without changing output. tsrs = oxc-project/tsrs pinned `=0.24.0`, linked in process via `tsrs_api::Session` (JSON text requests/answers; `crates/semantic/src/rpc.rs`, `checker.rs` 512 MiB stack thread).

Key numbers (shadcn apps/v4 cold, 2.06 s wall, 6.6 CPU-s): ~33.7k top-level requests + 17.9k in 4,060 batches; handler 1,776 ms of which `getSemanticDiagnostics` (one call, `instantiate.rs:182` probe file) 797 ms, `getPropertiesOfType` 546 ms (193 MB of 212 MB responses, 684/1,708 repeats). Codec ≥450 ms. Chakra: 743k `isReadonlySymbol` sub-requests, `batchRequests` 3.6 s; ~28k of 59k requests identical repeats. Unexplained 312-565 ms gap before first answer. Resolver ~20k calls for 1,385 files.

Items in order: 0 Chakra `isReadonlySymbol` in `Converter::fields`; 0b per-run (method, params) memo; 1 probe `getSemanticDiagnostics`; 2 `getPropertiesOfType` payload; 3 requests/component (mean 17.9), type-id memo, batching loops; 4 draft upstream issue (typed Response / leaner getPropertiesOfType) — owner sends it; 5 tsrs hot spots (SymbolMap rehash, JsonMap::get_index_of, NodeIndexTable, stat cache); 6 the 250 ms gap; 7 resolver memo per (dir, specifier).

Measure: corpora in ~/.cache/caliper/corpora/repos; `target/release/caliper-docgen extract --src <dir> --quiet --no-cache --load-dependencies --json` under `/usr/bin/time -l`; interleave main vs branch, best of 5-7, CPU time (user+sys), compare JSON minus `stats`; rerun a degraded run. Profiling: `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP=none REDACTED`, `sample caliper-docgen 8 1 -wait -mayDie`.

CORRECTION 2026-11-21: the JSON boundary is NOT the main cold-start cost. A prototype calling `dispatch::handle` directly (branch `spike/direct-dispatch`, byte-identical output) saved only ~2-4% CPU on shadcn and nothing measurable on Chakra; its sampled profile puts the codec at 2.0-4.5% of busy samples. An earlier "JSON codec 21% of busy CPU" figure came from a `sample` run that may have attached to another session's process (`sample` matches names by substring: profile with a uniquely named binary). Drop item 4 (upstream typed result) and any direct-checker rewrite for cold start; items 0, 0b, 1, 3 remain the leads.

Rules: no push/PR/upstream/merge; only small safe measured wins on own branch with failing-on-main test + CONTRIBUTING gate; no weekly oracle; build in worktree target/, delete multi-GB dirs after. Deliverable: report <700 words + table per item (measured, saving, effort, risk, order) + separate upstream issue draft. See [[run-the-oracle-sparingly]], [[measure-memory-and-time]], [[measurement-must-match-real-consumer]].

- It is a beta-labelled scheme: tsrs publishes about every 2-4 days now; the exact pin keeps us stable, but each bump re-triggers the toolchain question.

## 6. Recommendation

**Bump later** (on the next tsrs release that changes the checker/API, or when the MSRV moves for another reason). The bump is safe (builds without source changes, 206/206 semantic tests, byte-identical output on shadcn, Mantine and Chakra, no CPU/RSS change beyond noise), but it buys only edge-case module-resolution panic fixes and costs an MSRV 1.99 -> 1.100 change in CI, release and docs. If the owner wants the version scheme and the fixes now, it is a mechanical PR: Cargo.toml pins + rust-version, Cargo.lock, apps/oracle npm `tsrs`, CI/release toolchain, docs, then `just test-checker-lane` and `just gate-measure` in a real environment.

## Not verified

`just test-checker-lane` as written; the npm `tsrs` 7.1.0-beta.tsrs4 package and a parity run against it; `just gate-measure` determinism/memory modes; watch-mode memory over many edits; wall-clock or instruction counts (only CPU time under load 13-26); weekly oracle/corpus beyond the three named; other platforms (Linux CI); the GitHub release notes (API had a cert error, so only the commit log and crate sources were read); builds on rustc 1.99.1 are impossible (tsrs2+ need 1.100).
